title: Bias and fairness: where they come from and how to measure them

videos.script: Tarefa shortlists freelancers for every job. A system decides who a client sees first. {{title}} Nobody told it where anybody lives. It reads a rating, a count of finished jobs and a postcode. {{score}} The postcode is enough. In this lesson's lab, a freelancer in Recife misses a point that one in São Paulo gets for free. {{proxy}} The scorer that does it is a rule the course wrote, to behave like a model trained on who was hired before. {{standin}} You will measure the shortlist region by region. How often each group is chosen, and how often a good freelancer is passed over. {{metrics}} Then you will fix one of those numbers and watch another one break. When the groups differ underneath, no shortlist can be equal on all of them at once. {{tradeoff}} So choosing a metric means choosing who carries the errors, and writing that choice down. {{choice}} Last, you will change one field, keep everything else the same, and count the decisions that move. {{counterfactual}}
